question: Knowing what is known at the review date, would we write materially different protections for this borrower?

evidence_attributable_changes.rationale: Liquidity declined sharply, showing reduced buffer; evidence shows falling cash and availability.
evidence_attributable_changes.change: Increase the minimum liquidity threshold (require liquidity not less than a higher amount).

evidence.quote: Total Available Liquidity, defined as cash and cash equivalents, including restricted cash, plus availability under our short-term revolving credit facilities totaled approximately $196.1 million.
Total Available Liquidity, defined as unrestricted cash plus availability under floor plan credit facilities for inventory on hand at September 30, 2023, totaled approximately $73.6 million.

updated_summary: Liquidity has fallen from $196.1 million at end‑2022 to $73.6 million at end‑Q3 2023, eroding the buffer. No other covenant shows a material shift. Therefore only the minimum liquidity covenant warrants tightening.
updated_reasons: Evidence of declining liquidity justifies tightening the minimum liquidity covenant, altering risk coverage.
reading: Changes listed as evidence-attributable appear only when the new reports are supplied. Changes also present in the control reflect pre-existing gaps or model drafting preference, not newly emerging drift. One run of each; repeat-run stability is not yet measured.
